results.question: What does NVIDIA say about the impact of export controls in its latest 10-Q?
results.answer:
## Executive Summary
In its 10-Q for the period ended 2026-07-26, NVIDIA states export controls have and are likely to have a disproportionate impact on the company, potentially disadvantaging it against competitors selling chips outside the scope of such controls [S1].

## Key Drivers
Customers outside China and other impacted regions may "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors to reduce compliance burden and serve worldwide markets [S1]. Overseas governments may request customers purchase from competitors rather than NVIDIA or other U.S. firms, harming business and financial results [S1].

## Risks
The U.S. Government (USG) has already imposed export controls restricting certain gaming GPUs. Expansion of these controls could disrupt a significant portion of the supply and distribution chain and negatively impact sales outside China, including the U.S. and Europe [S3]. The French Competition Authority (FCA) is questioning whether gaming GPUs and data center GPUs are separate product categories, which may impact export controls applicable to gaming products in France and Europe [S3]. Increased performance of gaming GPUs over time may increase the impact of export controls on competitive ability [S3].
